headline: The last showers from Thursday's storm clear out overnight and by Friday morning, starting a mostly dry, noticeably cool stretch through early next week, with only a slight chance of light drizzle near the coast Sunday night and an uncertain storm possible around the Wednesday before Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thursday's weakening cold front has mostly moved through, after rain fell at 0.40–0.60 inch per hour at times and totals neared 1 inch on the coastal slopes near the LA County line. As of late Thursday evening a band of light to moderate showers was crossing southeastern San Diego County; scattered showers taper off Thursday evening farther north and by Friday morning in San Diego County, while low clouds west of the mountains, including the coast around Carlsbad, break up from west to east overnight. Gusty west winds on the desert slopes of the mountains weaken overnight, with bumpy, gusty air over and east of the mountains (including the Inland Empire) until about 4 AM Friday. Snow levels near 6,000 feet could leave about half an inch of snow around Big Bear Lake.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday turns mostly sunny by afternoon, though isolated light showers may linger over parts of the San Diego metro in the morning. It will be cool, with highs 5 to nearly 15 degrees below normal: only 30s and 40s in the mountains and 50s in the high desert. Saturday and Sunday stay cooler than normal with more clouds, as a weak disturbance moves through Northern California while another storm nears the Pacific Northwest.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Part of that weak disturbance may drift south and spin up over the desert Southwest, bringing a slight chance of very light showers or drizzle near the coast Sunday night into Monday morning; anything that falls will be light. Early next week looks dry and cool. Heading toward Thanksgiving, a large storm system over the northeast Pacific could either stay north as high pressure builds in from the south (dry and warmer here) or split, with part of it moving closer to bring potentially wetter weather around Wednesday; forecasters stress it is still about a week out, so check back.

coast: A building northwest swell keeps surf at 3–6 feet with sets to 7 feet on west-facing beaches through early Friday, with strong rip currents and minor coastal flooding during high tides (Beach Hazards Statement for the Orange and San Diego County coasts until 9 AM Friday). King Tides peak next week: tides above 7 feet are possible as early as Saturday, Nov. 21, and morning high tides may top 8 feet next Tuesday through Thursday, bringing widespread moderate impacts. For boaters, hazardous conditions last through Friday morning, with west winds gusting to about 30 mph (25 knots) and steep, choppy 5–8 foot seas Thursday evening slowly easing Friday morning; a Small Craft Advisory runs until 10 AM Friday for waters out to 60 miles from San Mateo Point to the Mexican border, including San Clemente Island. No further marine hazards are expected through Tuesday.
watch_for: Showers lingering in San Diego County until Friday morning.
King Tides: above 7 feet from Saturday and possibly above 8 feet on morning high tides next Tuesday–Thursday.
Whether next week's storm stays north (dry, warmer) or brings wetter weather around Wednesday before Thanksgiving.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the showers clearing out and the dry, cool stretch Friday into early next week, expect any Sunday night–Monday drizzle to be very light, and have low confidence in the midweek system ahead of Thanksgiving.
